Title: Kontoravdi et al. (2005) CHO growth and mAb model

Abstract: Fed-batch cultures are used in producing monoclonal antibodies industrially. Existing protocols are developed empirically. Model-based tools aiming to improve productivity are useful with model reliability and computational demand being important. Herein, a systematic framework for developing predictive models is presented comprising of model development, global sensitivity analysis, optimal experimental design for parameter estimation, and predictive capability checking. Its efficacy and validity are demonstrated using a fed-batch structured/unstructured model of antibody-secreting hybridoma cultures. Global sensitivity analysis is first used to identify sensitive model parameters (initial values estimated from batch cultures). Information-rich data from an optimally designed fed-batch experiment are then used to estimate these parameters, resulting in good agreement between simulation and experimental results. Finally, the model's predictive capability is confirmed by comparison with an independent set of fed-batch cultures. This approach systematises the process of developing predictive cell culture models at a minimum experimental cost, enabling model-based control and optimisation.

Laws:
(1) [balance] reactor liquid volume change equals inlet flow minus outlet flow
(2) [balance] viable cell mass balance accounting for growth, death and outflow
(3) [balance] total cell mass balance accounting for growth of viable cells and outflow
(4) [constitutive] specific viable cell growth rate equals maximum rate times limiting and inhibition factors
(5) [constitutive] product of Monod saturation functions for glucose and glutamine
(6) [constitutive] product of inhibition terms for lactate and ammonia
(7) [constitutive] specific cell death rate follows a Hill-type inhibition by ammonia
(8) [balance] glucose mass balance accounting for consumption by viable cells, inlet feed and outlet removal
(9) [constitutive] Specific glucose consumption rate equals growth‑associated consumption plus maintenance.
(10) [balance] Glutamine mass balance in the bioreactor.
(11) [constitutive] Specific glutamine consumption rate equals growth‑associated consumption plus maintenance.
(12) [constitutive] Maintenance coefficient of glutamine follows Michaelis‑Menten kinetics with respect to glutamine concentration.
(13) [balance] Lactate mass balance in the bioreactor.
(14) [constitutive] Specific lactate production rate is proportional to the specific glucose consumption rate via the lactate‑on‑glucose yield.
(15) [balance] Ammonia mass balance in the bioreactor.
(16) [constitutive] Specific ammonia production rate is proportional to the specific glutamine consumption rate via the ammonia‑on‑glutamine yield.
(17) [balance] balance of heavy-chain mRNA amount per cell
(18) [balance] balance of light-chain mRNA amount per cell
(19) [balance] balance of intra‑ER heavy‑chain concentration
(20) [balance] balance of intra‑ER light‑chain concentration
(21) [constitutive] rate of heavy‑chain consumption in assembly
(22) [constitutive] rate of light‑chain consumption in assembly
(23) [balance] balance of intra‑ER heavy‑chain dimer concentration
(24) [balance] balance of intra‑ER heavy‑chain dimer–light‑chain intermediate concentration
(25) [balance] Intra‑ER monoclonal antibody balance describing assembly from heavy‑chain dimer–light‑chain intermediate and transport to the Golgi.
(26) [balance] Golgi apparatus monoclonal antibody balance describing import from the ER and export to the medium.
(27) [balance] Secreted monoclonal antibody balance in the culture medium, with production from cells and removal by outlet flow.
(28) [definition] Definition of the specific productivity of monoclonal antibody as proportional to Golgi‑located antibody concentration.

answer.description: The model represents a fed‑batch CHO hybridoma culture producing a monoclonal antibody in a stirred‑tank bioreactor. It predicts viable and total cell densities, extracellular metabolites (glucose, glutamine, lactate, ammonia), intracellular mRNA and protein species, and the secreted antibody concentration. The model combines balances for volume, cells, substrates, products and detailed intracellular assembly steps, with constitutive rate laws for growth, substrate uptake, inhibition, and antibody biosynthesis.
